title: Open isolated copies and merge a selected immutable result through WorkspaceGuard
goal: Provide enforceable independent workspaces with a shared immutable base and a validated merge that preserves target ownership and all result history.
scope: Implement WorkspaceProvider CopyOnWrite and WorkspaceGuard.open(IsolatedCopy(base)) alongside Direct. Persist base snapshot/root/workspace associations and capture candidate changes without modifying the base, target or another copy.

Establish actual execution isolation for admitted producers and checks on supported macOS/Linux environments, including filesystem aliases, shared metadata and access to other candidate/hidden-check stores. A copied directory or declared write list alone is not an enforceable guarantee.

Implement kernel-validated merge(ResultVersion,target) with recorded selection input, target/base checks and path locks. Detect a changed target or conflicting paths before applying an invalid result; retain sufficient content/provenance to recover a failed/interrupted merge without reporting a partial application as complete.

Record ResultMerged and resulting Snapshot, keep non-selected candidates immutable, and release task-owned isolated resources only when their work/effects end while retaining the artifact/evidence content required by the journal.
acceptance: Two real admitted processes in distinct IsolatedCopy workspaces can make independent candidate changes; attempts to modify/read the other copy, target or protected hidden data are denied by the actual environment.

WorkspaceGuard merges a chosen result onto its applicable target and records exact before/after snapshots. A stale base, conflicting target change or failed merge leaves a truthful recoverable outcome and cannot be recorded as a successful complete merge.

Direct and CopyOnWrite run through the same real WorkspaceGuard consumer. Reopening the journal retains selected and non-selected results and does not grant authority to a provider-returned merge success.

Revoked/disconnected producers cannot cause a stale or unstable merge: scoped cessation/release evidence survives restart, financial settlement remains independent, and unrelated safe scopes are not globally blocked. Concrete observations implement R-19/R-20 without requiring new model-wide lifecycle abstractions.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, sections 3.4 (Workspace, ResultVersion), 4 (WorkspaceGuard.open/lock/snapshot/merge), 5.7 (WorkspaceProvider), A10/A11, principle 13 and R-9/R-16. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Create proposed runtime/workspace/copy_on_write.rs and kernel merge validation using W1 Direct snapshots/content/path locks and W3 scheduling. The materialization/isolation/merge mechanism is new implementation work; choose one concrete local approach with actual supported macOS/Linux enforcement.

A copied directory or declared path list alone is not an isolation guarantee. Verify target/candidate/hidden-store separation using real processes and refuse unsupported combinations. W4-0002 produces alternatives; W4-0003 owns policy selection.

WorkspaceGuard validates merge ownership/base/current target and persists exact ResultMerged basis. R-19/R-20 retain unresolved conflicting access independently of financial settlement; cleanup of isolated resources cannot delete retained result/evidence content.
